facts.statement: The genus Macrourogaleus was described by Fowler in 1947.
Macrourogaleus is a genus of shark that lived in the Late Jurassic Solnhofen Limestone.
facts.quote: Macrourogaleus is a genus of shark from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen Limestone.

facts.statement: Macrourogaleus had a slender body with a single dorsal fin and an elongate caudal fin.
facts.quote: The body is slender, with a single dorsal fin and a elongate caudal fin.

facts.statement: Macrourogaleus possessed a very elongate anal fin.
facts.quote: The anal fin is also very elongate.

facts.statement: The pectoral and pelvic fins of Macrourogaleus were noticeably rounded.
facts.quote: The pectoral and pelvic fins are noticeably rounded.

facts.statement: Macrourogaleus is closely related to Paraorthacodus and is placed in the family Paraorthacodontidae, though it was formerly classified in Palaeospinacidae.
facts.quote: It is closely related to Paraorthacodus, and placed in the same family Paraorthacodontidae, (though both genera were formerly placed in Palaeospinacidae)

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists Palaeospinacidae as the parent group for Macrourogaleus.
Macrourogaleus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Macrourogaleus lived during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 145.06 million years ago)
